lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p1-2 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details:
Listen and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound for the days of the week. Say practises first-step pronunciation. 
Practise builds accurate pronunciation and confidence with the target vocabulary through repetition.
Look for careful listening, clear pronunciation of each word sound, accurate word stress and confident repetition.
“I woke up so confused this morning. What day is it? Is it Monday? Thursday? Sunday? Help me remember the days of the week!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.103-104 - A Read and say

details: Read and say develops early decoding skills. Students blend sounds to read simple CVC words and practise recognising familiar phonics patterns before saying each word clearly and confidently.
Look for accurate blending, clear pronunciation, steady pacing, and correct identification of each word.
“I’m sure I’ve seen these words before but I don’t know what they say. Can you read them for me and draw a picture to match?”

Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down:

Draw reinforces comprehension of the CVC words by linking sound to meaning. Students show understanding through simple illustrations that match each written word.
Look for drawings that clearly represent each word, correct word–picture matching.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.103-104 - A Find 5 sight words

details: Find 5 sight words strengthens recognition of high-frequency words. Students scan the wordsearch to locate words quickly and accurately, preparing them for fluent reading.
Look for correct identification of all five sight words, careful scanning, and accurate transfer to the writing lines.
“You have helped me so much today! I just need you to do one more thing. This puzzle contains 5 words we use lots. Can you find them for me?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Write gives students controlled practice spelling the sight words they found. It reinforces whole-word memory, letter order, and neat handwriting.
Look for correct spelling, consistent letter formation, and neat handwriting within the lines.
